topic: planning classical compass-straightedge constructions and justifications
subtitle: Writing a construction as an ordered plan, justifying it with the congruent triangles the arcs create, and checking the finished claim on coordinates

problems.desc: Ordered plan for the perpendicular bisector of a segment: compass on A with radius more than half AB, arc on both sides; the same radius on B, arc on both sides; straightedge through the two arc intersections. Open plan -- check the ordering, the radius condition, and the compass placements.

Ordered plan for bisecting an angle: compass on the vertex, arc cutting both rays at P and Q; equal radii from P and Q meeting at R inside the angle; straightedge from the vertex through R. Open plan -- check the ordering and that the two later arcs share one radius.

traps.desc: added the horizontal and vertical differences instead of squaring, adding, and taking the square root

problems.desc: Justify the perpendicular-bisector construction: all four arc radii are equal by construction, so the two triangles formed by the segment endpoints and the two arc intersections are congruent by SSS, and CPCTC then gives congruent angles at the crossing point and equal halves of the segment. Open justification -- check that SSS and CPCTC are named and applied to the right triangles.

Ordered plan for a line through a point parallel to a given line by copying an angle: draw a transversal through the point meeting the line, copy with the compass the angle the transversal makes with the line to the same side at the point, then draw the copied ray. Open plan -- check that the copied angle is a corresponding angle and that the copy is a compass copy, not a protractor measurement.

Justify the equilateral-triangle construction: both arcs are swung with the compass still opened to AB, so AC and BC each equal AB because all radii of one circle are equal, and three equal sides make the triangle equilateral. Open justification -- check that the radius-of-a-circle argument is stated rather than read off the picture.

traps.desc: measured from the midpoint of the horizontal side instead of from the constructed circumcentre

problems.desc: Plan and justify the construction of the point one quarter of the way along a segment: bisect AB to get its midpoint M, then bisect AM to get the quarter point, justifying each bisection by the SSS equidistance argument, and explain why repeated bisection can never produce a trisection. Open synthesis -- check the plan, both justifications, and the limitation argument.
